title: Landmark Cars Ltd - 543714 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Landmark Cars Q4 FY26 reported revenue of INR 1,279 crore (+17% YoY) and EBITDA of INR 79 crore (+30%, 6.2% margin), with FY26 EBITDA a record INR 283 crore.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of consolidation, with growth coming from already-opened outlets and a focus on sweating assets rather than rapid expansion. Q4 proforma revenue rose 18% YoY to INR 1,795 crore and gross margin was 17.1%. Q4 PAT was INR 15 crore after exceptional write-offs for outlet closures and relocations. FY26 operating cash flow was about INR 267 crore and the dividend was raised to INR 1.5 per share from INR 0.50.

financial_highlights.value: INR 79 crore, margin 6.2% on reported revenue
INR 1.5 per share (subject to shareholder approval)

segments.name: New car sales
segments.commentary: Q4 new-car ASP was INR 23 lakh, up sequentially and YoY on higher-variant mix; FY26 ASP was INR 21.96 lakh vs INR 20.79 lakh in FY25. Mercedes-Benz ASP rose to INR 73 lakh in Q4 from INR 69 lakh in Q3.

segments.name: After-sales
segments.commentary: FY26 after-sales revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore at INR 1,051 crore (+12%). Average revenue per vehicle service was INR 30,072 in Q4 vs INR 27,420 in Q4 FY25; about 47% of service income comes from accident repairs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 is framed as a year of consolidation: no rapid store expansion, growth from Pune BYD outlets (July), Mahindra Hyderabad after-sales facility (July) and one or two other pipeline items.
Maintenance capex guided at roughly INR 50 crore, described as a ballpark rather than a firm number.
Management expects OEM price increases (FX and raw material driven, another hike expected in June) to lift ASP over time and give a one-time inventory gain; margin uplift described as marginal.
Management hopes for a better FY27 barring macro shocks; seasonality favours the second half of the year.
Interest-bearing debt fell INR 27 crore in FY26; further reduction expected, with long-term debt possibly needed if expansion resumes.
capex_capacity: Over the last 18-20 months the company built significant capacity; management now wants to sweat these assets.
Pune BYD sales and service outlets to be operational in July 2026.
Mahindra after-sales facility in Hyderabad to start operations in July 2026.
Kia workshop in Hyderabad operationalised in March 2026 and ramping up.
Store closures or relocations in Q4 led to exceptional write-offs; a Volkswagen location in a non-Gujarat state was dropped as unprofitable, while Gujarat VW dealerships continue.
demand_pricing: Industry grew about 13% in FY26 to 47 lakh passenger vehicles; April and May 2026 volumes were healthy. Commercial vehicles showed hesitancy in the last 8-10 days.
Most OEMs raised prices in April 2026 on FX and supply issues, with another hike expected in June; Mahindra, Honda, MG and Mercedes have taken or announced increases.

Mercedes V-Class (about INR 1.4 crore) and electric CLA (about INR 55 lakh) have waiting periods of a few months; top-end vehicles are about 20% of Mercedes sales. Management expects about 40 new Mercedes global launches, with India product flow from next year.

BYD supplies have been CBU; three models homologated (Sealion 7, Atto 3, eMAX). Q4 was constrained by an exhausted quota of non-homologated imports; management expects a better year under new quotas. Hybrids are expected later this year.

Kia New Generation Seltos has about a two-month wait; Renault Duster deliveries began mid-April with a hybrid expected at the festive season; Honda plans 10 launches; MG plans three new models; EVs are over 21% of Landmark's sales vs about 5% for India's passenger-car market.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and store expansion pace evolve over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Thakker said FY27 is a year of consolidation with no return to rapid one-shot expansion; the focus is on profitable growth and sweating existing assets. He did not give a margin target.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% after-sales margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10-year average is around 18%, and it urged investors to focus on the multi-year trajectory rather than a single quarter. The Q4 ASP rise was partly due to OEM bonuses and higher spare-part prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Thakker put the historical average at around INR 50 crore as a ballpark and said the company does not plan a large capex this year.

qa_highlights.question: Does EV penetration reduce servicing revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Thakker said accident repairs (about 47% of service income) cost more on EVs, which largely offsets lower routine servicing. He cited an older Goldman Sachs study showing a 12-14% after-sales revenue drop for EVs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise and how is it benefiting the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Days of inventory were 36 two quarters ago. The company held stock near 30 days ahead of price hikes and expected to return to about 30 days or lower; the benefit is selling existing stock at higher MRP.

qa_highlights.question: Will Volkswagen store closures affect the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one unprofitable Volkswagen location was closed and that Landmark remains VW's only dealer in Gujarat, where outlets are profitable.

risks_watch: Demand sensitivity to successive OEM price hikes and the war-related macro backdrop; commercial vehicles already showing hesitancy.
BYD supply constraints from the import quota system and the pace of CKD localisation.
Standalone profit volatility from Mercedes bonuses and target timing; Q4 standalone PAT rose to about INR 12 crore from about INR 7 crore.
After-sales margin normalisation (Q4 margin near 20%, against a stated 10-year average of about 18%) and EV-driven shift in service mix.
Ongoing store-level profitability reviews, including the Volkswagen outlet exit and outlet write-offs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the year's results and on the consolidation strategy, but evasive on quantified forward guidance (margins, ASP pace, after-sales margin and ROCE timing). Management repeatedly redirected quarterly questions to annual trends. Several answers were given on poor audio, and the transcript carries a disclaimed factual error on the FY reference.
key_quotes: So, this is the year of consolidation. We will grow this year with one or the other things that are already there.
So, it is a one-time gain for the stock that we are holding, not otherwise. It is a one-time gain.
I believe that what we have done on a consistent basis is what one should look at and not overtly look at this margin continuing.
